launches.body:
Hey everyone, we're the team behind [**mcp-use**](https://github.com/mcp-use/mcp-use), the open-source MCP framework with **10k GitHub stars** and **\~10M+ downloads**.

[**Manufact**](https://manufact.com/) is the cloud platform that gets your product onto the **Claude Connectors marketplace** and the **ChatGPT (Codex) Plugin Store** via MCP.

<https://youtu.be/Pyh_3tKDXuU>

## The problem

Paul Graham recently tweeted: "_AI apps are the new browsers_". \
Your customers now do most of their work inside Claude and ChatGPT, and the connector marketplaces are a new distribution channel: someone installs your product in one click and uses it inside the chat they already live in.

We listed Manufact on Claude and saw a **surge of signups** that is still going on now.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=107462&key=user_uploads/859771/65a0b3fd-75cf-4eea-a2ee-02590e3256ba)

But shipping a production-ready MCP server is its own project:

* MCP is a protocol evolving fast .
* Auth is easy to get [wrong](https://manufact.com/blog/authentication).
* Every client behaves differently.
* The stores have their own conformance requirements, and review can block you for weeks.

## How Manufact works

Manufact is the cloud built specifically for MCP:

* **Push to deploy.** Connect the GitHub App once and [every commit ships a new version of your MCP server](https://manufact.com/platform/hosting), with a preview deployment for each PR.
* **Test every MCP tool and MCP-UI widget** in the [cloud inspector](https://manufact.com/platform/cloud-inspector).
* **Know the moment your MCP breaks** in ChatGPT or Claude with [automatic cross-client testing](https://manufact.com/platform/cross-client-testing).
* [**Publishing checklists**](https://manufact.com/platform/publishing-checks) so your MCP app doesn't get stuck in marketplace review.
* **Auto-generated submission assets** (logo, copy, screenshots).
* **Analytics, session replay, and traces** built in for MCP, so you can see [how it's used and why tools fail](https://manufact.com/platform/analytics).

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=107462&key=user_uploads/859771/ee30e016-9fb5-4958-890f-74febc54de3c)

## Your product's UI inside the chat

A plain MCP server lets the agent read and write your data. \
An **MCP App** goes further: it's an MCP server that can return a UI as the result of a tool call, so your actual product interface renders inside Claude or ChatGPT. The user sees your charts and forms instead of a wall of text.

Ferruccio Balestreri (Amplitude) [put it well](https://x.com/0xferruccio/status/2028966278971670979):

> since mcp ui was released in claude we got a 2x boost in retention.

With the [mcp-use SDK](https://github.com/mcp-use/mcp-use) you write a normal React component, drop it in, and it registers as an MCP UI resource automatically.

## Backstory

We've been building on MCP since the protocol shipped. It started with the mcp-use SDK, the full-stack framework for MCP servers and apps. We kept watching companies struggle to take those servers to production, so we built the cloud for it (mcp-use is to Manufact what Next.js is to Vercel).

Manufact is now the **#1 recommended deployment option in OpenAI's docs.** 

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=107462&key=user_uploads/859771/ddba2350-67c4-43d5-8150-30847d4375a2)

We've helped startups from recent YC batches like **AgentMail** and **Item** get onto the Claude Connectors marketplace, and larger companies in finance, insurance, and marketplaces run their MCP apps on Manufact in production.

## Our asks

1. Have an MCP server? **Deploy it on [Manufact](https://manufact.com/)**.
2. Thinking about building an MCP App? [Copy our prompt for agents](https://manufact.com/prompt.md) and your coding agent will guide you.
3. Trying to get listed on the marketplaces? [Book a call with us](https://cal.com/team/manufact/chat). We have publishing checks and direct contacts on the MCP teams at Anthropic and OpenAI.

Hope to see your MCP on [manufact.com](http://manufact.com), or that you at least learned something new. 🙂

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=107462&key=user_uploads/859771/685643a6-ecd5-42b4-b55f-ec394967ca57)

launches.body:
### **TL;DR**

[Manufact](https://manufact.com) is the MCP cloud for dev teams to ship MCP Apps and Servers in production. Connect a GitHub repo and Manufact handles deployment, security, observability, and scaling, so teams can ship in minutes instead of weeks.

One codebase, deployed everywhere users and agents already live: the ChatGPT Apps Store, Claude Connectors, Gemini, Cursor, Claude Code, and more.

We're also the creators of [mcp-use SDK](https://github.com/mcp-use/mcp-use), the most popular high-level MCP framework for building MCP Apps and Servers.\
(mcp-use SDK is to the Model Context Protocol SDKs what Next.js is to React!)

It’s open-source and used by developers at 20% of US500 and companies like 6sense, Elastic, IBM, Innovacer, Intuit, NVIDIA, Oracle, Red Hat, Tavily, and Verizon are building with us.

### **The ask**

If you're building MCP Apps or Servers, or you know someone who is, we'd love to talk.

<https://cal.com/team/manufact/chat> \
or shoot a message to us: +1 (628) 899-2498 \
or [founders@manufact.com](mailto:founders@manufact.com)

### **Our story**

When MCP came out, we couldn't believe such a powerful protocol was locked into IDEs and Claude Desktop.

So we built mcp-use, the open source framework that lets any developer build MCP Apps and Servers in code, in a structured and composable way.

It got adopted fast: 7M+ downloads across Python and TypeScript, almost 10k GitHub stars, and dev teams at top companies shipping with it.

But OSS is only half the story. Once teams had something working, they hit the wall every infra team knows: deployment, auth, secrets, observability, scaling. Stitching that together for MCP is a multi-week project. That's what Manufact solves.

### **Make something agents want**

MCP unlocks something most products have never had access to before: real estate inside ChatGPT and Claude.

800M+ users already spend their day in those chats. \
With MCP, a product can show up there as a native app or connector, with no separate UI to build, no app to install, no new login flow. \
The user just asks, and your product does the work.

### **Problem**

The catch is that "build once, ship everywhere" is its own infra problem. ChatGPT Apps, Claude Connectors, Gemini, and the long tail of agent surfaces (Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, OpenAI Agents, Mastra, LangChain, Vercel AI SDK) each have their own quirks, auth flows, and submission requirements. Manufact lets you build one codebase and ship it to all of them.

### **What Manufact does**

Connect your MCP repo once. Every push auto-deploys.

1. **Build:** Scaffold a full MCP App or Server with _npx create-mcp-use-app_ or drop in existing MCP code unchanged.
2. **Deploy:** GitHub App connects once. Every push auto-deploys to Manufact Cloud. Preview URL per branch. Custom domains with SSL handled.
3. **Publish.** Get your app in front of users in the ChatGPT Apps Store and Claude Connectors. Submission assets, marketplace checklists, and an embeddable chat widget for your own site, docs, or campaign pages.
4. **Iterate.** Cloud Inspector debugs from any browser against real clients. Swap models. Run evals on every deploy.
5. **Monitor.** Analytics, session replay, JSON-RPC traces, and alerts on regressions, so you catch issues before users do. Less than 60 seconds from _git push_ to a live MCP App or Server, available across ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and any agent surface that speaks MCP.

### **Ask**

Do you know anyone already using MCP servers internally or building products powered by AI agents?

For the first few companies we will personally create/integrate MCP servers you need, have everything running through our platform, either on cloud or your own infrastructure. We even help you integrate our SDK into your code.

What do you think? Can we help you?

Book a call: <https://cal.com/team/manufact/chat>

Shoot a message to us: +1 (628) 899-2498 or [founders@manufact.com](mailto:founders@manufact.com)

launches.title: Bolna - Voice AI for India
launches.tagline: We enable Indian businesses to automate calls with multilingual, realistic Voice AI agents
launches.body:
Call our AI Agents at [+18722412481](tel:+18722412481) or [+912269539260](tel:+912269539260) to know everything about Bolna!

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Lq9ouROmRHA

**The Problem**

In India, phone calls remain the backbone of how businesses operate - from banks chasing loan repayments, to edtech companies qualifying leads, to e-commerce brands confirming deliveries. Millions of such calls happen every day. But the system is broken:

* **20+ Languages, 200+ Accents/Dialects**: Building a team that can handle all is impossible. Calls often switch mid-conversation (Hindi → Hinglish → Gujarati), and only a natural, adaptive AI can follow along and give a personalised experience to each caller.
* **Context-Dependent Requirements**: A delivery driver in Bangalore needs a low-latency, Kannada-capable model with high noise cancellation. A recruitment call to an engineer requires a slower but higher-quality reasoning model. There is no “one model to rule them all,” and integrating and managing 100s of models at scale is an unwanted hassle for businesses.
* **Cost Efficiency at Scale**: In India, every rupee matters. Voice AI must be engineered for efficiency - pre-recorded messages for common utterances, smaller vertical-focused models, and intelligent routing to minimize token usage.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=94216&key=user_uploads/1427127/bb2d0f37-0050-4606-8271-c8664a3d541b)

**The Solution**

Bolna is a **Voice AI Platform** purpose-built for India’s scale, linguistic complexity, and cost sensitivity. We enable enterprises to go live with thousands of concurrent calls in days, not months.

* **Enterprise-grade performance**: Sub-500ms latency, interruption handling, multi-language (10+) and accent (50+) adaptation, fluent in natural multi-language conversations (Hinglish, English + Tamil etc.)
* **India-specific routing**: Bolna automatically picks the optimal model blend for the context, regardless of language, region, or use case.
* **Cost-efficiency engine**: Calls are optimized with pre-recorded inserts, cheaper small models where possible, and routing logic that prioritizes ROI without sacrificing experience.
* **Complete control**: Enterprises define workflows, tone, and intelligence. Bolna handles everything behind the scenes.

launches.body:
Hey YC, we are [Aman Mishra](https://www.linkedin.com/in/aman005/) and [Adnan Abbas](https://www.linkedin.com/in/adnan-abbas-903b711a2) from [Unsiloed AI](https://www.unsiloed.ai/).

**TL;DR:** _Unsiloed AI is building the most accurate APIs for ingesting multimodal unstructured data like PDFs, PPT, DOCX, tables, charts, and images, and converting it into structured Markdown and JSON for downstream LLMs and AI Agents._

We are already processing millions of pages of complex documents each week for Fortune 150 banks, NASDAQ‑listed companies, as well as early‑stage startups in accuracy-sensitive domains like finance, legal, and healthcare.

https://youtu.be/ULDK5dgfgzM

**The Problem**

More than **80% of enterprise data is multimodal and unstructured**. AI teams spend **6+ months** building accurate document‑ingestion pipelines that keep breaking.

* From the tons of open‑source solutions out there, it’s still tough to achieve superior accuracy on even mildly complex cases.
* Traditional OCRs are static and break with changing layouts.
* LLMs, although good at comprehension, suffer at **deterministic extraction**, making them unreliable for accuracy‑sensitive domains like finance and healthcare.
* Early‑stage vertical AI teams end up becoming **document AI companies**, reinventing the wheel, as evident from **300+ conversations** we’ve had with AI teams of all sizes.

**Solution (What we built)**

We combine **vision models** with **OCR‑based models** to accurately extract information from complex documents.

**1) Pre‑processing & Segmentation**

* We segment data into **texts, tables, images, and plots** using specialized models for each task.
* We use a **heatmap‑based chunking** technique that first generates **pivot elements** from the document. Pivot elements are the elements of importance, e.g., **numbers and merged cells in tables**.
* This chunking strategy ensures all related pieces of information are preserved in the **same chunk** (e.g., a table spanning multiple pages, rows split across pages), while unrelated information is split across chunks. The result: retrieval feeds **only accurate, complete‑context chunks** to LLMs.

**2) Dual‑Stream Representation**

Post pre‑processing, we pass the segmented chunks through **two parallel streams**:

* **Data Stream:** preserves the **extracted content**.
* **Layout Stream:** preserves the **actual layout & hierarchy** (indentation, alignment, clause/sub‑clause structure).

This matters because the data is not just text and numbers the **structure carries meaning** (e.g., a right‑aligned cell in a financial table or the way clauses/sub‑clauses are arranged). The dual stream captures both **semantic content** and **structural cues**.

**3) Domain‑Specific Decoder**

* A decoder consumes both the streams and structures the outputs as per the required **JSON schema** or **Markdown**.
* We incorporate **domain‑specific ontologies** (finance, healthcare, legal).
* An in-built **RL pipeline** to train the decoder when outputs involve internal terminology that is hard to capture using a general LLM.
* We generate **confidence scores** for each extracted item; **low‑score items** are collected over time to run **fine‑tuning jobs**

We can run all of this under fully air-gapped on-premise environments as well for privacy-sensitive verticals.\
\
**Here are some sample outputs generated by our Vision Models:**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=95076&key=user_uploads/879419/fdfed5e7-994a-47d3-9357-b20b1d2a3b67)

JSON output from handwritten, scanned docs, along with confidence scoring and citations.\
\
**Our Progress:**

We are already processing millions of pages for Fortune 150 banks, NASDAQ‑listed companies, as well as early‑stage startups (including 10+ YC startups) across finance, legal, and healthcare. On public benchmarks, we consistently outperform solutions from LlamaIndex, Gemini, Mistral, and [**Unstructured.io**](http://Unstructured.io)**,** among others.

**Our Ask:**

Parsing **PDFs, images, PPTs,** or **Excel files** for your **Vertical AI** use case or **RAG** pipeline? Give [**Unsiloed AI**](https://www.unsiloed.ai/) a try. We turn months of ingestion work into one API call for every document type.\

Coding agents made every developer faster. But the platform team did not get faster with them.

Developers now ship with Cursor/Claude/Codex and generate infrastructure, deployments, and provisioning requests at a rate no platform team was staffed for.

At illumio I once waited more than three weeks just to get Kafka clusters provisioned for a new service I was building. And provisioning is only part of it. The platform team is also on the hook for incident response when production breaks, repairing the CI/CD glue that ties the deployment pipeline together, platform security, and every "can you just" developer request in Slack.

Most platform teams pick one of two bad options. They hand developers (and their agents) direct access to infra, CI/CD, and cloud accounts, and hope nothing breaks. Or they gatekeep and become the bottleneck every developer has to wait on.

Building a platform that developers actually like has been a luxury only the largest engineering orgs could staff, and an understaffed platform effort usually does more harm than good.

Platform teams use Kestrel to automate incident response, cloud provisioning, CI/CD, security, developer requests, and more across their stack. name: s2.dev
long_description:
S2 is an API for durable streams. We make working with streaming data dead simple and reliable.

The more we worked on data systems, the more we felt like there was a missing building block. The seamless experience of object storage simply did not exist for durable streams – so we set out to fix that!

S2 reimagines streams as an unlimited and access-controlled web resource. Like if Kafka and S3 had a baby.

- Building agents? Use granular streams to persist context in real time, make workflows auditable, and coordinate between agents.

- Publishing fast-moving data? Streams support high fanout and can be accessed directly over the internet, so they are a great fit for broadcasting real-time feeds.

- Sandboxing? Emit to per-instance streams, and read history or live events just as easily.

- Local-first and multiplayer experiences? Propagate updates reliably and efficiently.

Stop dealing with clusters, and start streaming.

launches.title: s2.dev: Streams as a cloud storage primitive
launches.tagline: The serverless API for unlimited, durable, real-time streams
launches.body:
Hi everyone! We are [Shikhar](https://www.linkedin.com/in/shikhrr/), [Stephen](https://www.linkedin.com/in/stephen-balogh-078a4995/), and [Dwarak](https://www.linkedin.com/in/dwarakgovindparthiban/), the co-founders of [s2.dev](http://s2.dev). S2 is the S3 for streams.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8-mUPf4P_8g

Many of the most important features in products we love are powered by streaming data, from frontend UIs that go _brrr_ with real-time updates, to backends that store and process massive event flows. But building these sorts of real-time systems is really hard.

We are turning streams into a cloud storage primitive – just like object storage did for static files.

S2 is a completely serverless datastore, offering unlimited streams and configurable (even bottomless) data retention. Streams can be appended to and followed in real-time, and since all writes are durable, you can also read from anywhere in a stream’s history, indexed by sequence number or timestamp.

We basically took the core abstraction of Kafka – [the log](https://engineering.linkedin.com/distributed-systems/log-what-every-software-engineer-should-know-about-real-time-datas-unifying) – gave it a URI, and brought it online with a dead simple API. And none of the bloat. 😀

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2a1OdJ9l78A

## Why we’re building S2

We built large-scale ML infra at Etsy and Meta, and always felt the lack of a system like S2. Serverless infra for data at rest has been seamless for a long time (S3 launched 20 years ago!) – but the ecosystem around streaming data, in comparison, felt stuck in the stone age.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=95319&key=user_uploads/235940/72f8cb1e-a550-4458-b57b-d5936dc98191)

When we [first introduced S2](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=42480105), we thought it would be most attractive to people already using streaming platforms like Kafka – but we’ve found that it resonates much more with builders in areas where these systems are entirely absent, who end up cobbling together general-purpose stores like Postgres and Redis and run into their limits.

We stand out on dimensions that are completely off the map for legacy systems: like the ability to have an unlimited number of streams backed by object storage, and to make them directly accessible [over REST](https://s2.dev/docs/rest/records/overview). This means S2 streams can be used as a serverless, reliable alternative to custom WebSocket or SSE infra.

## S2 radically simplifies streaming

If you are dealing with a **high-cardinality of data sources** – for example, code execution sandboxes or IoT devices – S2 is for you. Streams can be instantly created on-demand. You don’t have to buffer or batch, just pipe into S2.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wsFiwxv_RY0

We recently [supercharged](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=45310294) read scalability to handle massive fanouts. You can broadcast a **real-time feed** with S2 such as market data without building any infra – publishing is just a matter of POST-ing to a stream’s URL.

If you are building **agents**, a common pain is **syncing** progress between the backend and frontend, while also being able to replay history. A lot of these agent state management challenges become simple with S2.

## Try it out

We should talk if [s2.dev](http://s2.dev) resonates with you! You can [sign-up](https://s2.dev/sign-up) and follow the [quickstart](https://s2.dev/docs/quickstart) to start streaming in seconds with free credits.

There is a lot more we are cooking, including an ⭐ open source self-hostable S2 https://github.com/s2-streamstore/s2 ⭐

**discord**: https://discord.gg/JfTWJ5xxZ6

**twitter**: https://x.com/s2_streamstore

launches.body:
**TL;DR:**

Lemma is the first evaluation + observability platform built not just to measure performance, but to improve it automatically. We help AI agents learn from real user feedback and production data, closing the loop so your prompts and agents continuously optimize themselves over time.

**Launch Video:** https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=E4_v-pY_4fs

Hey everyone! We’re [Jerry](https://www.linkedin.com/in/jerry-n-zhang/) and [Cole](https://www.linkedin.com/in/colegawin/), co-founders of [Lemma](https://www.uselemma.ai/) (YC F25).

**The Problem:**

**AI agents don’t learn from their mistakes. In fact, they get worse with use.**

In production, prompts and agents continuously degrade due to real-world input drift (new user behaviors or unseen edge cases). Agent performance can often **drop \~40% in a few weeks**, and suddenly what worked in testing breaks in front of customers.

When that happens, engineers are forced to dig through logs, collect failing examples, and manually tweak prompts rather than building core product features.

**Solution:**

That’s why we built **Lemma: the first end-to-end system that closes the loop between agent deployment and improvement.**

**Here's what that means:**

**Step 1:** Lemma detects failed outcomes directly from live traffic, and it automatically identifies the exact cause in an agent chain.

**Step 3:** We give you back an improved prompt and automatically open a PR in your codebase so your prompts can live where you want them. Alternatively, you can also fetch your prompt from the Lemma dashboard.

**Plus, Lemma provides all the LLM eval and observability features you rely on, just reimagined for continuous learning:**

* Agent tracing observability with live drift detection, regression alerts, and performance visibility across real user interactions.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=95219&key=user_uploads/1798805/2b82ecee-1965-4fc0-831d-36b76db3f064)

Teams using Lemma cut manual prompt iteration by 90%, resolve production drifts in minutes instead of days, and improve model performance \~2–5% every optimization cycle.

**Our Story:**

We met freshman year at USC and have been building together ever since instead of going to classes.

Before starting Lemma, we were engineers at two high growth, AI-native startups: Tandem (AI for healthcare) and Chipstack (AI agents for chip design). At both companies, setting up evaluations looked like clunky Retool dashboards and multiple engineers manually tweaking experiments. We built internal systems that automated both running the evaluations themselves, as well as the error-driven feedback loop. The result: 2x accuracy improvement and speed of iteration.

We soon realized every AI company was reinventing the same internal tooling in-house. So we left college, joined YC, and are now bringing continuous learning infrastructure to everyone else.

launches.title: Amika - the operating system for AI agents to write and verify code
launches.tagline: Run fleets of human-in-the-loop or background coding agents inside cloud computers. Let them automate coding and verify it's correct.
launches.body:
Software isn't a craft anymore, it's a manufacturing problem.

At Amika, we're building **the open source operating system for coding agents to automate their work**, like how the factory automated manufacturing.

**Amika gives each agent a cloud computer, and lets you build automated or human-in-the-loop workflows for agents to write code and prove that the code is correct.**

A couple of examples:

\- Have Amika monitor production and auto-fix errors, testing the fix against your real app

\- Add Amika to shared customer Slack channels. Auto-implement customer requests and share a live preview the updated app with them

Check out some more examples in our video 👇

<https://youtu.be/GxqFsiBNbww>

# The problem

AI coding agents made code generation cheap. Producing correct code at scale, with real quality controls, is still unsolved. You're left with a tradeoff: pore over every change and go slow, or vibe-code and ship slop.

Coding agents are useful, but the surrounding system is missing.

\- They lack the right **dev environment to verify their work**

\- They lack the right **context to understand the full problem**

\- They lack **deterministic guardrails controlling what they can change**

\- They produce 10x more code, but teams lack **a system for 10x more review**

# How Amika solves this

Amika composes 5 primitives into its agent operating system:

1\. **Sandboxed environments**: isolated cloud computers with the repos, tech stack, MCP servers, skills, and context an agent needs.

2\. **Workflows**: programs as code or markdown files that define when an agent runs and what job it does.

3\. **Deterministic guardrails**: rules enforced on every code change, like "do not cross this module boundary" or "every database query must include a customer ID filter."

4\. **Automated verification**: test, review, fix, and merge loops that check the work against your real tech stack before it ships.

5\. **Audit trails**: the agent chat session, code changes, which checks passed, and what the run cost.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=103929&key=user_uploads/101903/a1246cf3-1ed1-435d-94fb-2cb7437b4995)

Amika works with your existing coding agent subscriptions (Claude Code, Codex, etc.) so **you're not locked into one vendor**. Start agents from the web, Slack, GitHub, the CLI, or the API. At any point, a human can take over the sandbox and inspect the running apps, or drive from their own code editor.

Because each sandbox runs your full stack, you review the agent's work in a live preview of your real app, plus the verification artifacts it produced, like screen captures or API test requests, instead of poring over the diff line by line.

With Amika's workflows and environments, you can spend time building higher level loops for your agent to write and verify code, speeding up your product development.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=103929&key=user_uploads/101903/60e16093-3dcf-4285-b73b-998c74507145)

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=103929&key=user_uploads/101903/3b84372e-0a00-46a3-afd1-d711547c256b)

We pivoted our YC company to bet on this, and we already use Amika for the majority of our PRs. We're building it in the open: each primitive ships as open source, and our cloud platform packages the whole operating system into a software factory for teams.

launches.title: OneTriangle - The fastest, cheapest inference, powered by KV cache transfer
launches.tagline: Lightweight novel inference
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** OneTriangle is building the cheapest, fastest inference. We cut inference prefill costs by 20% and time-to-first-token by 40%, letting you get large-model quality at small-model cost.

Video: <https://youtu.be/HKe2EZUdNHo>

**Team**

We’re Hannah (CEO) and Medha (CTO), MIT CSAIL grads building with a team of 4 MIT engineers spanning ex-DeepMind and Jane Street, Physics and Astronomy Olympiad medalists, and NeurIPS/ICML authors. 

**The Problem**

Inference is expensive. 

• You’re forced into a bad tradeoff. You need the decoding power of large models, but you have the budget for small ones.

• Prefill is the hidden tax. For long-context and agentic workloads, prefill dominates cost and latency, and everyone just eats it.

**Our Solution**

OneTriangle transfers the KV cache between models, something that has never been done in production. We prefill on a small model, strip the positional encoding, map the cache into the large model’s space, and restore relative importances. The result:

• 20% lower prefill costs

• 40% faster TTFT

• Large-model quality at small-model cost

We beat out NVIDIA’s KV cache transfer paper by getting a lower KL divergence score in 2 weeks.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=111487&key=user_uploads/2573695/e64727d6-a7b1-404a-bfbb-22ad2b941142)

\
No API changes, no quality cliff, and we’re upstreaming it into vLLM so the fastest path to cheap inference is the infrastructure you already run.

**Why Now**

Inference has surpassed training as AI’s largest compute cost, and it’s accelerating with demand for agents that generate 10x the tokens a chat session does. Inference already eats up to 90% of total compute cost, over $600 billion is going into AI data centers this year alone. Every team pushing the frontier is bottlenecked by the same thing: serving costs.

\
**The Future**

Our bet is that model-mixing becomes the default serving pattern: small models handle prefill and routine tokens, large models handle the hard ones, and the cache moves freely between them. Whoever owns the transfer layer owns the economics of inference. We are the future of lightweight, fast inference.

launches.body:
We're [Sanchit](https://www.linkedin.com/in/sanchitmonga22/) and [Shubham](https://www.linkedin.com/in/shubham-malhotra-fg890a23a/), co-founders of [RunAnywhere](https://runanywhere.ai/) (W26).

**TL;DR:** Run Multi-modal AI fully on-device with one SDK and manage model rollouts + policies from a control plane.

We are already live and open source with [**\~10.1k stars on GitHub**](https://github.com/RunanywhereAI/runanywhere-sdks).

<https://youtu.be/N3x2bs4ri68>

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97041&key=user_uploads/725397/86d47939-7caf-4e0f-8575-045ca2fd22bc)

### The Problem

Edge AI is inevitable — users want instant responses, full privacy (health, finance, personal data), and AI that actually works on planes, subways, or spotty rural connections.

But shipping it today is brutal:

* Every device (iPhone 14 vs Android flagship vs low-end) has wildly different memory, thermal limits, and accelerators.
* Teams waste quarters rebuilding model download/resume/unzip/versioning, lifecycle (load/unload without crashing), multi-engine wrappers (llama.cpp, ONNX, etc.), and cross-platform bindings
* No real observability — you're blind to fallback rates, per-device perf, crashes tied to model version

**Result:** most teams either give up on local AI or ship a brittle, hacked-together experience.

### The Solution: Complete AI Infrastructure

RunAnywhere isn't just a wrapper around a model. It is a full-stack infrastructure layer for on-device intelligence.

**1. The "Boring" Stuff is Built-in** We provide a unified API that handles model delivery (downloading with resume support), extraction, and storage management. You don't need to build a file server client inside your app.

**2. Multi-Engine & Cross-Platform** We abstract away the inference backend. Whether it's llama.cpp or ONNX etc, you use one standard SDK.

* iOS (Swift)
* Android (Kotlin)
* React Native
* Flutter

**3. Hybrid Routing (The Control Plane)** We believe the future isn't "Local Only"—it's **Hybrid**. RunAnywhere allows you to define policies: try to run the request locally for zero latency/privacy; if the device is too hot, too old, or the confidence is low, automatically route the request to the cloud.

![Voice AI Pipeline Demo](/media/?type=post&id=97041&key=user_uploads/725397/dfe1b180-e5d8-4c59-a4e8-2109d9f903f2)

### Quick Links

launches.tagline: We deliver low-latency, low-cost AI inference by eliminating the memory wall using full-stack optical interconnects and a purpose-built software stack.
launches.body:
**The Problem: The Memory Wall Is Breaking the Economics of AI Compute**

AI’s promise is unprecedented, but its economics are broken. Copper-based interconnects cannot keep up with modern models, limiting data movement between and within compute and memory. The result is high latency, inefficient hardware utilization, and unsustainable inference costs—creating a hard ceiling on AI margins.

---

**The Solution: Grow-Style Optimization for the Interconnect**

Today’s data-center compute and networking were not designed for inference. Slow, power-hungry **copper** interconnects, along with costly signal processing and memory overhead, drive high latency and high cost.

High-performance inference requires purpose-built hardware and a vertically optimized software stack. Piris Labs builds this optimized stack by combining proprietary **optical** interconnects with software designed to maximize hardware utilization. We vertically optimize the interconnect layer—just as the compute layer was vertically optimized by **Groq** (acquired by **NVIDIA** for $20 B).

Piris Labs combines proprietary optical interconnects with a purpose-built software stack designed to maximize hardware utilization, delivering **5x** lower latency, **10x** lower power per bit, and **2x** lower cost per token\
\

* Ali Khalatpour: MIT-trained engineer and Harvard–Stanford–trained optical scientist; developed the first room-temperature terahertz semiconductor laser; led the development of GUSTO’s optical engine for NASA

launches.title: Salus - Runtime guardrails that validate AI agent actions before they execute
launches.tagline: Salus checks your agent's actions, blocking incorrect ones and providing feedback to guide retries
launches.body:
### **TL;DR:**

**Salus is an API that wraps around your agent and checks its actions at runtime, blocking incorrect ones and providing immediate feedback to guide retries.**

We’re Kevin and Vedant, former roommates at Stanford who studied CS, now building Salus full-time.

### 😔**The problem:** 

Your agent processed a refund without looking up the order, costing you thousands. It emailed your top lead using hallucinated data, ruining the deal. You only found out three hours later from a support ticket or an angry email.

Evals, output scoring, and observability are all necessary—but all reactive. They can reduce the likelihood of these problems occurring, but there's no solution that inspects an action as it’s about to execute. Salus does that.

**Ask:** If you are deploying agents and want to improve their correctness we’d love to help. Book a demo [here](https://calendly.com/d/cycy-fbc-fyj/salus-demo), and we can onboard you immediately with just a pip install and a few lines of code.

### 💻 **Our Solution:** 

<https://youtu.be/uyl5NJTY5Cg>

**How Salus validates an action:**

1. Actions must be **grounded in evidence**: Salus maintains an evidence cache for each run that every proposed action is validated against. Evidence includes all outputs from prior tool calls and the entire conversation history.
2. It must **adhere to policy**: Write constraints in YAML, markdown, or plain English. Salus compiles them into runtime checks that are version-controlled, diffable, and shadow-testable
3. And **more**: PII detection, budget/loop protection, idempotency, human-in-the-loop escalation, content moderation

**Self-repairing:** When Salus blocks an action, the agent receives structured feedback to guide a retry. In our benchmarks, **58%** of blocked actions recover and complete the task correctly.

### 📊 **Benchmarks:** 

We tested Salus on τ²-bench and ODCV-Bench. On τ²-bench, agents with Salus follow policies more reliably, at up to **60% lower cost**. On ODCV-Bench, Salus **reduced misalignment by 52%** on average across 12 frontier models (see below).

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=97574&key=user_uploads/1940292/e48b27f6-2e13-4d40-a9a4-13135ff981bc)

### ➕ **Other Features:** 

While we believe the missing piece is runtime validation, we know **evals and observability** are crucial. That’s why we incorporate all three in **one centralized product**. Using templates and LLMs, we generate thousands of both adversarial and realistic evals that have full context of your agent’s domain.

Contact us: [founders@usesalus.ai](https://founders@usesalus.ai)

launches.title: Fern – Realtime Socially Aware AI for Meetings
launches.tagline: Fern joins every meeting as–either invisible copilot or active participant–so every conversation runs like a top 1% professional
launches.body:
**TL;DR**\
[Fern](https://www.ishikilabs.ai/download) is a realtime AI that joins your meetings as either an invisible copilot or an active participant– your choice! It realtime proactively coaches you through every conversation so you always show up like a top 1% professional.

Hey everyone, we're Amit and Robert, cofounders of Ishiki Labs.

**The Problem**

_“AI meeting assistant” has become synonymous with a note-taker waiting to summarize at the end. That's not a meeting assistant. That's a fancier transcript._ 

Building a realtime AI meeting copilot is hard in two distinct ways.

The invisible assistant must understand the live meeting context at blazing speed and surface the right thing at the right moment – questions to ask, things you're missing, who you're talking to. Timing is everything. Current AI is purely reactive. Making AI an active participant in discussion is even harder. AI has no social awareness – every pause becomes a prompt, every gap an invitation to speak.

AI that is socially aware and proactive is an unsolved problem. That's what we're building.

The cost of this gap is real. Cofounders, AEs, recruiters, investors – in discovery calls, sales meetings, investor conversations. The moments that matter most, and AI is absent from all of them.

**How Fern Solves it**

[Fern](https://www.ishikilabs.ai/download) joins your meetings as a true participant or an invisible copilot – your choice. It has two modes:

**Full Presence**: Fern joins visibly, listens, and speaks up when invited. It offers realtime opinions, deep research, and can complete tasks like filing notes or sending emails on the spot. Built for internal product, engineering, and strategy meetings. Watch the demo- <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vRJfZDUHvSY>

**Shadow Mode**: Silent and invisible to everyone else. You get a private realtime feed: live summaries, questions to ask, things you're missing, context on who you're talking to. A sharp colleague whispering in your ear – with fully customizable insights. Built for client calls, investor meetings, and any conversation where you want invisible support.

Both modes include a post-meeting summary, transcript, and full insights.

**Team**

We're both ex-Meta. Amit is an AI Scientist from LLaMA (now Meta Super Intelligence Lab) and Reality Labs – PhD in AI, 20+ publications at NeurIPS/CVPR, trained multimodal assistants for smart glasses. Robert was systems and infra lead in Reality Labs, with four years building low-latency multimodal systems at Meta and Citadel Securities. 

Our mission: make AI socially timed and contextually aware – so every conversation you have runs like a top 1% professional.

**Our Ask**

Download [Fern](https://www.ishikilabs.ai/download) and if you're a founder or AE who lives in high-stakes conversations and don’t want to settle for AI note-takers, reach out: [team@ishikilabs.ai](mailto:team@ishikilabs.ai)

launches.body:
> **TLDR:** Create an API sandbox with the environments your CI, tests, and evals need. Your coding agent can start the API sandboxes (e.g Linear, Slack, Datadog), run tests, and inspect state changes. Ask your agent about archal.ai!

Hi everyone, I'm Aidan, the founder of Archal. I previously built agent environments at Scale AI and I've been an avid developer for most of my life, which led me to the problem Archal poses to solve.

[https:/youtu.be/pUfu1RFDYVk](https://youtu.be/pUfu1RFDYVk)

**What we found**

Coding agents are getting much better at writing integrations, but testing those integrations is still painful. Many providers do not offer a usable sandbox, so developers fall back to throwaway accounts, shared test workspaces, or thin mocks. Those options are difficult to reset and make it hard to know whether an agent actually completed a task or only returned a plausible response.

As Adam Bender at Google put it, “But with 10x more code and 10x more services, integration tests are going to become the most important part of your quality strategy.” (Google, Software engineering is at the tipping point)

**How Archal works**

With all of this in mind, I built Archal for a starting point of how the next generation of devs will do QA. It's a tool focused on giving agent developers and integration engineers API sandboxes of the SaaS platforms they use in prod pipelines. With Archal, a developer or their coding agent can start a sandbox, run the task, inspect what changed, and reset everything for the next test. We eliminate the need of separate test accounts, thin mocks and stubs, as well as overburdening rate limits on provider-owned sandboxes.

**Our ask**

We're giving out $20 in Archal credits to each new developer that signs up and starts a sandbox. We’d love for you to give it a try and give us feedback, cheers to making testing easier in the era of coding agents!

AI labs require massive, high-quality video data to train multimodal models, but clean, custom video datasets cost millions and take months to collect.

**Ask;** If you or someone you know runs physical operations (manufacturing, logistics, retail, security) and wants to automate visual tasks without buying new hardware, we’d love to connect!

**Our Launch Video:**

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=36OaIJ4FPZ8>

**Our Team:**

OpenVector was founded by a team of builders and engineers obsessed with bringing self-improving visual intelligence to the physical world.

* [Andrey Gizdov](https://www.linkedin.com/in/andreygizdov/), CEO, dropped a fully-funded **PhD** scholarship from Fulbright, worth **$170,000**, with invitations at **Harvard and MIT**, where he worked on real-time vision models.

**Problem**:

Many important business moments happen in the physical world: Someone tailgates. A production cycle stalls. A worker skips a step in the manufacturing process. A customer arrives, and no one responds. There are over 1 billion cameras worldwide, but they only record it for later. For physical operations, the best technology available to catch these events in real-time has been a human staring at a monitor.

**Solution:**

OpenVector is an AI that brings action to any camera.

* **Plain English to AI Model:** No coding or expensive setup. Simply describe your task in plain English, and OpenVector automatically builds the best AI vision model for it, and watches your camera feeds 24/7. It’s an app that takes 2 minutes to download and set up, and works with any camera.

* **Legacy Integration:** It automatically integrates with your existing systems to make a call, send an email, update your POS or CRM, or trigger a webhook the second an event happens.
* **Zero New Hardware:** Works entirely with the cameras you already have installed (custom end-to-end solutions also available).

**We’ve Already Started:**

OpenVector is already live and seeing use cases across security, retail, manufacturing, and logistics. We are tracking production cycle efficiency directly from existing CCTV, ensuring good-manufacturing-practices, and catching physical design errors.

**Now Onboarding:**

OpenVector is ready to deploy on your camera feeds today. Contact us if you’re tired of cameras that only watch and want them to actually do work for you. [founders@openvector.com](mailto:founders@openvector.com)

launches.tagline: Leveraging a global human network to collect data that don’t exist yet.
launches.body:
Hub provides real-world training data to frontier AI labs and robotics companies. We went to 7-figure revenue agreement on data delivery during the last weeks, working with some of the biggest names in AI and robotics.\
\
**Why now**

The gap between frontier models is closing, and internet-scale data is largely exhausted. The only edge left is real-world data that humans have to produce. Every lab now wins or loses on its edge cases, and edge cases need specific data captured by specific people: data that doesn't exist anywhere online. Whoever can go collect the right data first ships the better model first. Human labor is half of global GDP, and almost none of it has been recorded yet.

**What Hub does**

We capture this data through a global network of humans, across all continents. We route and activate the exact people who fit a lab's brief and deliver in days, not the months it takes to source a generic dataset off the shelf. Because we collect the data ourselves, we can attest its provenance, which you can't do for data you didn't capture. Our ML and QA pipelines then verify and enrich it, so we meet the hardest dataset requirements labs throw at us. The moat isn't the data, it's how fast we can go get it.

**Traction**

From 5-figure to 7-figure in revenue agreement on successful data delivery. We now work with some of the biggest frontier AI labs and robotics companies in the world.

**The ask**

Two asks: —> You're building frontier models or robots and data is your constraint. \
—> You're a top robotics engineer, a PhD whose research touches robotics or egocentric data, or someone with deep experience at a leading robotics lab, we're hiring. \
\
Reach out here: [founders@hub.xyz](mailto:founders@hub.xyz).

launches.title: Expanse - Unlock wasted GPU capacity
launches.tagline: Unlock wasted GPU capacity.
launches.body:
**TL;DR**

Expanse unlocks wasted GPU capacity. We’re the intelligence layer for compute infrastructure. Submit jobs with the right resources. Optimise them to run faster. Debug failures in seconds, not days. Works on cloud and on-prem HPC.

Want to know how much more you can get out of your hardware? Schedule a call: <https://book.getexpanse.io>

**Problem**

Running compute on a cluster means guessing memory, time, and GPUs before you submit. Get it wrong and your job fails mid-run. Over-guess and you pay for compute you never use. 30% of cloud spend is lost to over-allocation \[1\]. Microsoft Research found their own deep learning jobs hit 50% GPU utilisation or lower \[2\].

Sizing jobs takes decades of experience. Memory patterns, batching, GPU threading, CPU vectorisation. AI agents don’t have enough information to fix it either. SLURM and Kubernetes don’t expose enough structured data. Even strong platform teams are forced to choose: spend time debugging and optimising every job, or accept the waste. AI infrastructure spending will hit $2.52 trillion in 2026 \[3\]. The waste grows with every new cluster. This problem isn’t going away.

**Solution**

Expanse learns your cluster. We analyse your code and hardware telemetry, then track them over time. Our deep learning models build a picture of what your workloads actually need. Predictions get sharper with every job.

Our models are deployed on your cluster. All analysis runs on your network. Your code and telemetry never leave your infrastructure. We can’t see your data, and you maintain full data sovereignty.

One command installs Expanse on your cluster. You get two tools.

`expanse analyse` - for every job:

* **Suggests the right resource configuration**
* **Predicts failures from historical code and telemetry patterns**
* **Surfaces code-level optimisations that increase efficiency**

`expanse diagnose` - for every failure:

* **Finds the root cause**
* **Returns solution-oriented logs with the exact code and config changes to fix it**

Days of debugging and optimising become seconds. Platform teams get what they need to do this in minutes instead of weeks.

**Founders**

We're four engineers from the University of Edinburgh, all coming from top quant funds and national supercomputing centres. Ismaeel built the first multimodal HPC resource predictor at EPCC (Edinburgh's Parallel Computing Centre), beating every published baseline. Yafet built the first GNN cluster graph network for predicting SLURM queue wait times. Eren built decentralised foundation model training systems at Edinburgh. Niko trained large-scale speech ML models on GPU clusters and architected cloud and Kubernetes infrastructure at one of the largest hedge funds in the world. We left our jobs to fix this ourselves.

**CTA / Ask**

Running compute and not getting enough out of what you’re paying for? Failing jobs, unclear errors, bills too high? We’d love to chat.

Know anyone in AI infrastructure (managing cloud and/or on-premise data centres), quant finance, drug discovery, or AI research labs? An intro would mean a lot :)

**YC Deal**

All YC companies running serious ML training can contact us for a discounted pilot. We’ll find inefficiencies and wastage on your compute setup. Then we deploy Expanse, no changes to your workflows. You get more out of the hardware you’re paying for.

Reach out: [founders@expanse.sh](mailto:founders@expanse.sh) or <https://book.getexpanse.io>

References

\[1\] <https://grafana.com/blog/2023/03/03/how-to-optimize-resource-utilization-with-kubernetes-monitoring-for-grafana-cloud>

\[2\] <https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/publication/an-empirical-study-on-low-gpu-utilization-of-deep-learning-jobs/>

\[3\] <https://www.gartner.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2026-1-15-gartner-says-worldwide-ai-spending-will-total-2-point-5-trillion-dollars-in-2026>

launches.title: InsForge: The backend platform for AI-native developers
launches.tagline: Let your coding agent deploy, operate, and debug your backend end-to-end
launches.body:
Hey YC! We’re [Hang Huang](https://linkedin.com/in/hang-huang-oliver) and [Tony Chang](https://www.linkedin.com/in/tony-chang-0430/) from [InsForge](https://insforge.dev/).

**TL;DR:** InsForge lets your AI coding agent deploy and operate the full backend (servers, database, auth, storage, and more) from one consistent CLI. Instead of stitching together separate tools and dashboards, your agent manage entire backend infrastructure end-to-end.

<https://youtu.be/7Bax5qz0IfM>

**The Problem**

The way software gets built is changing fast. Coding agents are now the primary builders, but every backend platform today was designed for human developers, with dashboards, manual configs, and workflows that require a person at every step.

We tried MCP servers like Supabase, Vercel, GitHub, and Context7, but kept running into the same problems: tools bloated the context window, payloads came back at 10K+ tokens, and core backend state like telemetry, configs, logs, and runtime behavior still wasn’t accessible in a way agents could reliably use.

**Our Solution**

So we built InsForge as one backend platform your coding agent can actually operate. Install our CLI and Skills with one command, and your coding agent can build, run, debug, and scale full-stack apps end to end on InsForge.

Every primitive returns structured outputs and readable errors the agent can act on. And because agents make mistakes, branching, scoped permissions, and reversible writes let you review or discard changes safely.

**Where We're Going**

We believe that coding agents won’t stop at writing code. They’ll run your entire application and infrastructure autonomously as well. For that to work, backend infrastructure needs to become agent-native: CLI-first, observable, permissioned, reversible, and designed around agents as operators.

**About Us**

name: Rindler
long_description:
We build Maxxwell, a desktop app for people who run several coding agents at once.

Past two or three sessions, you become the bottleneck. Every session asks you something, most of it small, and you spend the day answering instead of deciding. It is also hard to tell which sessions are making progress, which are stuck on something trivial, and which have quietly started building the wrong thing.

Maxxwell puts every session in one window and marks each one working, idle, or waiting on you. On top of that sits an orchestrator, a real coding-agent session of its own that reads the others and reports back. You talk to it instead of to twelve terminals. It tells you what landed, what it decided for you, and what actually needs your call.

Every worker is your own tool, unmodified. Claude Code, Codex and Cursor Agent run in real terminal sessions you can attach to and take over at any point

launches.title: Rindler - Turn Any Website Into An API For AI Agents
launches.tagline: Reliable web actions for AI agents, without integrations or scripts
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** Rindler turns websites into deterministic APIs for AI agents. We map a site once into screens, actions, and structured outputs, so agents can read data and take actions quickly and reliably.

**Ask:** If you’re building an agent that needs to browse the web, compare products, fill forms, search listings, use authenticated portals, or act on third-party websites without an API, we’d love to help.

<https://youtu.be/V_nCIxYD-so>

## Problem

More products are starting to depend on AI agents that can do real work on the web: shop across retailers, pull housing listings, use job boards, submit forms, monitor prices, update back-office systems, and operate inside customer portals.

But most browser agents still treat every website visit like a new puzzle. On every run, they need to decipher the page, infer what matters, decide what to click, and recover when the page behaves differently.

That works for demos, but it breaks down in production. Real websites have pop-ups, login gates, cookie banners, bot defenses, slow-loading forms, dynamic filters, fragile dropdowns, layout changes, and pages that look similar but behave differently.

The result is slow execution, high token cost, and workflows that are hard to trust.

## Solution

Rindler maps websites into deterministic APIs for agents.

Instead of forcing an agent to re-explore a site every time, Rindler captures the site as structured screens, available actions, and typed outputs. Agents can then call actions like **search,** **add_to_cart**, or **download_records,** depending on the mapped site.

At runtime, Rindler handles the browser work through a remote MCP endpoint:

* Returning structured data
* Applying dynamic filters
* Managing popups, bot defenses, and layout changes
* Supporting authenticated flows

## Background

We started Rindler because “AI agent uses a browser” is compelling, but the current browser-agent loop is too brittle for teams building real products.

If an agent needs to use the same third-party site hundreds or thousands of times, it should not have to rediscover that site from scratch on every run.

Rindler is still a work in progress. Some sites map cleanly, others require more in-depth mappings, and bot-defended or logged-in sites may need a one-time credential or cookie capture.

We’re looking for feedback from founders building products where reliable web actions are part of the core workflow.

If there’s a website you wish your agent could use reliably, send it to us!

name: Riften
long_description:
Intelligence will be the most valuable asset a company owns. Today, almost every company rents it.

Companies pay a handful of labs one token at a time. Each dollar buys an answer, not an asset. They spend more, but own nothing more.

Riften reverses that.

Change one environment variable and Riften becomes the gateway for a company's AI traffic. We route each request to the lowest-cost model that can do the job, serving most work on open-weight models we host. Customers save money immediately without rebuilding their products.

The gateway is the entry point. Over time, Riften turns the company's work into private models built on open weights and shaped around the business. What begins as cheaper inference becomes an intelligence stack the company owns, runs on infrastructure it controls, and uses to power its most important applications.

We call this earned intelligence. It is created by the company's own work, controlled by the company, and accumulated over time.

The next generation of companies will not rent their intelligence. They will earn it, own it, and compound it. Riften is how they get there.
one_liner: Earned intelligence for every company

launches.title: Riften: Route every AI request. Build the models your company owns.
launches.tagline: Cut LLM spend with one endpoint that selects the lowest-cost model that works.
launches.body:
[Riften Launch Video](https://youtu.be/9T82XHysqsc)

## What Riften does

Riften is an OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible gateway that routes each LLM request to the lowest-cost model capable of completing it.

Connect your existing providers, change the base URL, and keep the product you already built. Riften works across customer-facing AI products and internal tools, including Claude Code and Codex.

**Riften is already removing enterprise-scale model spend from production workloads.**

## Why we built it

Most AI products choose a model once and send nearly everything to it.

A documentation lookup, a support classification, and a codebase migration do not require the same intelligence. Yet they are routinely sent to the same frontier model at the same price.

For customer-facing products, that cost cuts directly into gross margin. For internal agents, it limits how broadly the company can deploy them.

## How it works

Riften evaluates each request locally, applies the company’s cost, capability, latency, and reliability constraints, and selects among the models available to that organization.

Hard tasks can still reach frontier models. Routine work moves to lower-cost commercial or open-weight models. Teams can keep their provider accounts, pin a specific model when needed, and inspect the cost and routing decision behind every request.

The objective is not the cheapest token. It is the lowest expected cost of completing the work.

## From routing to company-owned models

The router reveals which work is repeated. Outcomes reveal whether it was done correctly.

A passing test, an accepted patch, a resolved ticket, or a completed workflow can become part of a customer-specific evaluation. Riften uses those evaluations to improve routing, post-train open models around recurring work, and test those models against the APIs they are intended to replace.

Models earn production traffic through the same endpoint. Frontier APIs continue to handle novel work. Repeated workloads move onto models the company controls.

That creates a direct path from inference routing to evaluation, post-training, deployment, and the applications where the work happens.

The model labs are building intelligence every company can rent. Riften is building the path to intelligence every company can own.

## Team

Riften is founded by Carl Stauffer, a former Palantir Forward Deployed Engineer who shipped software into the purchasing and production systems of a nine-figure manufacturer. He was Palantir’s first Neurodivergent Fellow through Alex Karp’s program, conducted nuclear research at Jefferson Lab, studied computer science and applied mathematics at Johns Hopkins, and is an a16z Scout.

The rest of the team comes from Stanford Mathematics, Berkeley computer science, and Carnegie Mellon mathematics and computer science. Their work spans Oxford OATML, SPAR, CMU CyLab, Palo Alto Networks, Millennium, Amazon Search, NASA, UCSF Health, and industrial manufacturing systems.

They have built agent orchestration platforms, LLM evaluation and fine-tuning systems, cryptographic security software, production search infrastructure, CAD-matching systems, and autonomous QA for measuring agent performance. Their research includes an ICML acceptance and current work in review at NeurIPS.

The team also brings national-level recognition in mathematics and technical research spanning manufacturing, computational science, and new energy systems.

Riften combines enterprise deployment, frontier evaluation research, competitive mathematics, agent systems, security, and production ML in one team built for the full path from request to outcome to model.

## The ask

**We are looking for companies with meaningful LLM usage across customer-facing products or internal agents.**

If most of your traffic still runs through one frontier model, send us:

* Your current default model
* Whether the traffic is internal or customer-facing
* Your approximate monthly model spend or volume

We will show you what should remain on the frontier, what can move today, and whether Riften is worth testing.

Email us at [info@riften.ai](mailto:info@riften.ai).

launches.body:
**TL;DR:** AI hardware trades over phone calls and forwarded spreadsheets. No venue, no price to mark against: lenders mark billions in GPU collateral off appraisals. We're building Stoa, an RFQ marketplace where buyers and sellers get firm quotes within 48 hours, and settled trades build the prices the market can mark, finance, and hedge against.

<https://youtu.be/zbD21BgAo88>

GPU deals close in group chats. We know because we've been in them.

A price arrives as a voice note. Someone forwards an inventory list, then it gets forwarded again, and soon three brokers are offering the same machines. Nobody knows who actually owns what or whether any quote is firm.

The market behind those chats is worth hundreds of billions of dollars a year. Lenders mark billions in GPU collateral off appraisals, not trades.

We're Berat, Eren, and Kaan. We're building Stoa.

AI hardware is becoming an asset class, but its market is missing the basics: a venue where hardware can trade, prices that buyers, sellers, and lenders can mark against, and eventually financing and hedging built on those prices. We're starting with the venue: an RFQ marketplace for GPUs. It gets buyers and sellers firm quotes, and every bid and settlement builds the history the rest needs.

**Here's how it works**

Post what you want to buy or sell: B300s, H200s, H100s, a bare card or a full cluster, new or secondary.

Vetted dealers bid blind with firm quotes. Instead of spending weeks calling around, you get through the RFQ in 48 hours.

We handle the unglamorous parts too: KYB and counterparty checks, contracts, shipping, and settlement.

In our first month, $300M+ in RFQs ran through the book.

**Why the marketplace comes first**

Ask what an H100 is worth and everyone you call gives you a different answer.

On Stoa, dealers quote against the same RFQ without seeing each other's bids. Because every RFQ, firm quote, award, and settlement runs through us, we see what the hardware actually trades for.

A quote is an opinion. A settled trade is a receipt.

That transaction history becomes prices buyers, sellers, and lenders can mark against. Once marks are grounded in settled trades, financing and hedging can follow.

Platts started printing oil prices in a magazine. Kelley Blue Book began as one dealer's published list of what he'd pay for cars. GPU inventory is still being passed around in forwarded spreadsheets, and Blackwell upgrades are now pushing H100 fleets into the secondary market.

Someone is going to be the price.

**The team**

We've known each other for more than ten years. We have founded companies, traded interest rate derivatives, and built trading and pricing infrastructure for oil and gas. Now we're building it for AI hardware.

**Buying or selling?**

If you're buying GPUs or compute, or you're sitting on hardware, sign up at [stoaexchange.com](http://stoaexchange.com).

**Schedule a call: [https://stoa.cal.com/stoa/intro](https://stoa.cal.com/stoa/intro)**

**Text or call us:** +1 510 605 3844

And if you know infrastructure heads at neoclouds or data centers, hyperscaler capex teams, dealers, ITADs, or credit desks lending against GPUs, please send this their way.

launches.body:
**TL;DR:** We are building a market for future inference capacity. You buy tokens for a model over a time window from the provider of your choice at a price fixed today (up to 30% off - or more for larger orders via direct quotes). If your plans change, you will be able to resell your reserved capacity to another buyer.

<https://youtu.be/nMaDr46NU5I>

**Problem**

Token spend is growing and it’s growing fast. Out of 100+ companies we spoke to, most are trying to cut their inference costs.

Reserved capacity guarantee deals provide discounts + certainty, but are negotiated bilaterally, take time, and are **hard to switch from** - as a buyer you commit by prepayment, which you lose if you switch to a different provider, or in some cases even a different model.

What if a buyer could:

1. See all possible discounted capacity deals in one place
2. Buy with a click of a button
3. Have an option to resell to another buyer with another click of a button

**But why would model providers (sellers) want this?**

In short:

1. Model providers’ goal is to maximise GPU utilization - the more information they have about future demand, the better they can allocate capacity.
2. Selling future capacity is an excellent way to finance GPU compute - dilution-free and interest-free
3. Extra distribution channel for enterprise buyers

**What if a new model comes out but I already bought capacity for the older one?**

Contracts for “Best model in class” allow you to buy frontier model capacity in advance. And even if you're holding a contract on an older model when a new generation ships - far from every application needs the frontier, so you can list your capacity for resale.

**What if I am a _very large_ buyer and these discounts are not enough?**

We are launching Requests for Quotes (RFQs) - as a buyer you can create a request for capacity you need and let providers bid to offer you the best price.

**Team**

Ilia: Maths & Finance @ Imperial, Product (Wealth & Trading) @ Revolut

Roman: CS + Math @ NUS, IOI gold, 2x Quant Research @ Citadel Securities, AI engineer @ Lovable

**If you're a company buying tokens or a model provider, email us at [contact@touchmark.ai](mailto:contact@touchmark.ai) or sign up at[ https://app.touchmark.ai/signup](https://app.touchmark.ai/signup)**

_Capacity transactions on Touchmark are limited to commercial producers and commercial end users in the wholesale capacity market. Sellers offer capacity to Buyers that purchase it to consume or use in connection with the Buyers' commercial operations. Some contracts are available only in the primary markets._

launches.tagline: Field Robots Faster with ATC Deploy
launches.body:
Today we're sharing Agency Tool Company and our first product, ATC Deploy: a faster, more reliable way to ship software to robots wherever they are. It moves updates up to 20 times faster than docker pull or scp and works with any software stack already in use.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jx0rLRVa06s>

## The updates that took until 2 a.m.

Davis and I spent eight years building Scythe Robotics and putting hundreds of autonomous mowers to work across the country. For years, we deployed software with a tool I'd cobbled together for our first few robots. As the fleet grew, deployment became an ordeal: engineers stayed up until 2 a.m., we coordinated with customers to move robots out of sheds and into LTE coverage at set times, and failed transfers restarted from zero. Shipping a fix could take more coordination than building it. We had models to train and customers to serve, so the tooling limped along with incremental bandaids.

We've since heard the same story from robotics teams across industries. That deployment becomes a hidden bottleneck: teams become release-averse, feedback loops slow and improvements stall. Stitched-together web and IoT tools barely work if you know which scripts to run and who to call, so they survive, even if it means every update is distracting from improving the product.

## What we built

ATC Deploy ships whatever you already run: OS images, Docker images, or any file tree. Run “atc ota push user@robot”, and it sends only the changed bytes, then restarts your software through hooks you define—way faster than a docker push.

Install takes one “curl | sh” command and a config file so you can get back to work fast. Interrupted transfers resume where they stopped, and an offline robot can receive updates by USB if you need. There's no new runtime, packaging format, or operating system to adopt.

## Shipping to robots today

ATC Deploy already ships software to robots at Burro, which has deployed more than 750 machines worldwide, Tempo, polishing concrete across several US states and Canada, and Gather, who is scaling their 99.9% accurate inventory drones nationwide. Their teams spend less time managing delivery and more time improving the robot.

**Operate a robot fleet? Join the ATC Deploy waitlist at [agencytool.com](https://agencytool.com/).** Know a team that should be using it? Send them this post, or to [mailbox@agencytool.com](mailto:mailbox@agencytool.com).

It's time to build robots.

launches.body:
# \*\*\*\*

**TL;DR: We're building a modern tax engine for accountants and fintechs building on tax: a deterministic tax calculation and e-filing core behind a single API, built on the IRS's official e-file infrastructure (MeF).**

## A tax return is math. It should be a function call.

We're Angelo and Akash, and we built Luca IQ, a new tax engine for accounting firms. One set of inputs in, a completed, filed return out in minutes. Not bolted onto decades out desktop software.

For CPA firms, that means more returns per preparer, less spend on labor, and a clean path off 30-year-old desktop software. For the PE groups acquiring and scaling firms, it means real operating leverage on the single most labor-intensive part of the business.

<https://youtu.be/IV5nl7grMxI>

**The problem.** \~95% of US firms file their returns through just four companies, and all of them were built decades ago, for the desktop, and are closed. Firms are stuck running tax season on software that can't scale with them. Every modern AI tax tool just pushes data into that same closed software it can't control. Everyone rebuilt the interface.

**What we built.** A new one, and we're opening it. A key principle: AI never does the tax math. AI and human judgment set the inputs, and a deterministic engine computes the return, with a full audit trail on every number. It's either 100% correct or it's wrong, and only a deterministic engine can promise the former. For firms, that means throughput without giving up accuracy or defensibility.

Our core leverage: we're an **IRS-authorized e-file provider as a Software Developer, Transmitter, and Intermediate Service Provider**, so Luca IQ doesn't just compute the return, it e-files straight to the IRS. That full path, calculation through filing, is what firms can't get from a closed engine today.

**Why now.** The profession is running out of people. 300,000+ accountants have left since 2019, and \~70% of CPAs are near retirement. At the same time, private equity is rolling up firms and pushing hard on margin. The work isn't going away. The people are, and the pressure to do more with fewer preparers has never been higher.

**Who we are.** Angelo (CEO) is a CPA who worked in forensic accounting with the FBI, Wall Street, EY and spent years working at tax firms using the legacy softwares we are now replacing. Akash (CTO) was employee #1 at a fintech data-infrastructure startup and leads engineering.

**What we need:**

* **CPA firms who dread tax season**, We'd love 20 minutes to show you what Luca IQ does for throughput and margin. This is who we build for.
* **PE firms rolling up accounting practices.** If tax prep labor is your biggest cost line, let's talk.
* **Developers and fintechs** who need 1040 calculations or e-filing. The engine is one API call, and you can build on it early.

Reach us at [founders@lucaiq.com](mailto:founders@lucaiq.com).

launches.body:
**TL;DR:** Inkbox is the identity and communication layer for AI agents: giving agents their own email, phone, iMessage, and internet address. Inkbox pulls together what your agent sees across email, calls, iMessage, and more, so your agent can act on the full context.

Hey YC! We're Ray, Alex, and Dima building Inkbox.

**How we got here**

A few months ago we were building web-automation agents. Every time an agent needed to log into a portal, it had to receive a confirmation email or get a 2FA code. And when we were away from our desks, we wanted to seamlessly contact the agents themselves: text them, check in, get a reply. We ended up stitching together services like Gmail, Twilio, and ngrok: separate services, each built for humans, none of them sharing any identity or context. 

That's the problem we set out to fix. We didn't need another email or voice API. We needed one service to tie its identity together with rich context. So we built it.

[**Launch video**](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oJKl6tPHxRA)

**What Inkbox does**

Our API gives every agent:

* A unique email inbox (+ custom domain)
* A phone number that can call and text
* iMessage
* A persistent internet address (HTTPS tunnel) to receive internet traffic, like webhooks
* An encrypted credential vault with TOTP/2FA

**Who we are**

* Ray (CEO): CS PhD from MIT; previously cofounded Empallo, an AI virtual clinic for cardiovascular patients.
* Alex (CTO): MS in CS @ Northeastern. Previously ML engineering and computer networking research.
* Dima (CAIO): built ML pipelines on gigapixel pathology images at Harvard Medical School; co-author on 6+ peer-reviewed publications.

[**Quick demo with Claude**](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MTVkW_EG-Y4): Watch Claude Code provision an email, phone, and iMessage in a Minute.

**Our ask**

* **Try it**. Drop Inkbox into your preferred agent harness: we have plugins for[ Hermes](https://github.com/inkbox-ai/hermes-agent-plugin),[ OpenClaw](https://github.com/inkbox-ai/openclaw-plugin),[ Claude Code](https://github.com/inkbox-ai/claude-code-plugin), and[ Codex](https://github.com/inkbox-ai/codex-plugin). Each one runs a wizard that provisions Inkbox resources for your agent.
* **Ask your agent to self signup**. _Sign up for an Inkbox email account by following the guide at[ https://inkbox.ai/docs/get-started/agent-signup.md](https://inkbox.ai/docs/get-started/agent-signup.md) and refer to[ https://inkbox.ai/llms.txt](https://inkbox.ai/llms.txt) for full documentation._
* **Intros**. We'd love intros to teams running fleets of agents that each need their own identity to act in the real world: reaching out to people and businesses (email/phone/iMessage), holding their own accounts, and authenticating with a built-in credential vault.

Contact Ray at [ray@inkbox.ai](mailto:ray@inkbox.ai). Would love your feedback.

name: Decawork
long_description:

Access decisions need to adapt in real time as the agent works, but companies can’t turn every business judgment into a fixed rules or have people manually approve every step.

We train small, company-specific models that approve AI actions in real time. They consider the company’s policies and interests, the agent’s current task, and its past actions to decide whether each proposed action should be allowed. Access is specific to the task at hand and reassessed as the agent works.

Companies will rent intelligence from AI labs or run open-source models to power their agents. They’ll own the models that keep their entire AI workforce acting in their interests. Decawork is building those models.

launches.title: Decawork - Training company-specific models that approve every AI action
launches.tagline: Our small AI models decide agent access in real time, task by task, based on your company’s interests.
launches.body:
Hi everyone 👋 - we're Aman and Sarthak, founders of Decawork.\
\
**TL;DR:** AI agents shouldn’t have permanent access to company systems. The same action can be appropriate for one task and wrong for another, but companies can’t turn every business judgment into fixed rules or manually approve every step. Decawork trains small, company-specific AI models that approve every agent action in real time, based on company policies and interests, the agent’s task, and its past actions. Access is granted for the task at hand and revoked when it’s done.\
\
Launch video: [Watch it here](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SanpHIyFcV4)\
\
🚧 **The Problem & Why now?**\
Companies are putting long-running, more autonomous agents to work on broader tasks and goals. These agents need access to critical company systems, but their actions can be unpredictable and may not serve the company’s interests.

OpenAI’s agents have already hacked Hugging Face during testing with reduced safeguards. Replit’s agent deleted data from a live application’s database.

An agent’s access should depend on the task it is doing. The same action can be appropriate for one task and wrong for another. Permanent access lets an agent keep using permissions even when they are no longer appropriate for its task.

As agents take on more work independently, access decisions need to happen in real time. But companies can’t turn every business judgment into a fixed rule or have people manually approve every step.\
\
✅ **How we solve this?**\
Decawork gives AI agents access for the task at hand and revokes it when the task is done.

* Connect your agents. Route API requests and MCP tool calls through Decawork to see activity and manage access in one place.
* Set company policies. Write policies in plain English, specify when human approval is required, and connect your existing identity and IT service management systems.
* Deploy a company-specific policy model. We deploy small models that approve actions in real time using your company’s policies and priorities, task context, and past actions. Your agents do the work. Decawork evaluates each proposed action and enforces the access decision before it runs.

🚀 **Team**\
Sarthak built AI systems at NVIDIA that were deployed at OpenAI and Meta, and worked on enterprise AI agents at Ema.

Aman built the AI compliance platform at Barclays used by internal teams globally, then led product at a consumer AI startup serving 100K+ monthly users, hand-wiring credentials for the agents he shipped.

Every one of those deployments came down to the same questions: what can it access, who approved it, and what did it do? We kept solving agent access by hand - so we quit to build the system we wished we’d had.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=109883&key=user_uploads/1632535/0ef2784e-ab45-422f-91b9-960473f11dd5)

🙏 **Our Ask**

* If you’re on an IT team or know someone who’s worried about AI agents accessing or misusing company systems, talk to us: <https://decawork.ai/cal> or [founders@decawork.ai](mailto:founders@decawork.ai)
